packets.title: Preserve local Telegram cancellation and unspecified flood-wait diagnostics
packets.finding: The final CLI error mapper turns a local Ctrl-C UsageError into generic ConnectionError. A flood_wait with no positive retry duration also loses its wait-specific guidance.
implementation_contract: Preserve local prompt cancellation using fixed safe wording and the existing cancellation/usage classification, including when a provider adapter wraps the prompt exception.
Keep duration-specific guidance for a positive safe retry_after; retain the wait class without inventing a duration when it is absent or unusable.
Leave provider error sanitization, connector authentication, cooldown persistence, retries, app credentials and source enrollment architecture unchanged.
Retain generic fallback for unknown exceptions; do not forward all Error/ConnectionError/provider messages.
normal_acceptance: At phone, code and password prompts, ordinary local cancellation produces the fixed cancellation diagnostic and UsageError classification consumed by existing CLI dispatch; no success output or new connection is recorded and normal cleanup runs.

Map a classified flood_wait with retry_after=120 to duration-specific wait wording; map the same code without a usable duration to wait-specific wording with no fabricated count or immediate connectivity retry advice.
An ordinary unreachable error still uses the existing generic connectivity diagnostic.
Existing unknown prompt-error sanitization, missing app credentials, successful enrollment and cooldown tests retain their assertions.
validation: Qualified root runner executes the new helper tests and relevant normal enrollment/cancellation tests on the exact candidate.
Apply required CLI/type/full repository checks and independent exact-change review; product/native/account qualification remains separate.

packets.title: Allow uninstall of a known enabled and inactive service without restarting it during rollback
packets.finding: The real query produces state=disabled, enabled=true for a known inactive enabled systemd unit. changeService accepts only active+enabled or stopped+not-enabled, so both uninstall and reinstall refuse that normal state.
implementation_contract: Represent the known pre-change runtime activity independently from enablement for the normal stopped-but-enabled systemd case.
Permit uninstall from that state while still disabling and verifying both stop and disabled enablement before removing the owned unit.
Do not redefine confirmedStopped to accept enabled units.
Preserve prior inactivity during recoverable failure restoration; current enable() starts/restarts, so merely widening admission is insufficient.

Retain backward-compatible reading/recovery of version-2 service-change journals. An internal journal extension must explicitly preserve the prior activity and enablement semantics; no SQL/schema migration is in scope.
Retain unknown-state refusal, owned-definition checks, service identity, existing active-service recovery and truthful pending-recovery errors when restoration cannot be verified.
Keep the implementation limited to the systemd stopped/enabled correction; preserve launchd behavior and optional host-adapter compatibility.
normal_acceptance: A fake supervisor with independent state and enablement starts active+enabled; after an ordinary stop it reports inactive+enabled; uninstall disables it, removes its unit, writes opted-out intent and preserves all ordinary vault content.
An already inactive+disabled unit and a normal active+enabled unit remain uninstallable.
Ordinary unsuccessful disable/reload/restore responses preserve or truthfully report recovery state and never start a previously inactive service.
An ordinary known inactive+enabled service can be reinstalled using the existing activation contract if that shares the corrected transaction admission.
Existing version-2 normal rollback/recovery fixtures continue to work; existing unknown-state refusal remains.
validation: Use synthetic SupervisorHost/service-command fixtures only in the qualified test runner; do not operate systemd, launchd or a daemon during implementation.
Run focused supervisor and CLI install tests, typecheck and required repository checks; independent review must assess journal compatibility and prior activity restoration.
P091 subsequently owns actual Linux native install/stop/uninstall and vault-preservation qualification.

packets.title: Expose safe Claude import health warnings without redefining ingestion totals

implementation_contract: After root freezes the reporting contract, expose a bounded and explicitly labeled health warning on stderr for initial and repeated Claude imports with ordinary unsupported parts.
Retain invocation event totals and ingestion error counts on stdout; parse issues remain distinct from event-write errors.
Preserve the existing successful partial-import exit behavior unless root separately approves changing it.

Do not claim that a fresh health observation is the exact captured snapshot; if snapshot-bound reporting requires a new public connector/core contract, return that gap rather than widening this write grant.
normal_acceptance: A clean ordinary two-message Claude file imports successfully with two stored events; unchanged repeat stores zero.
An ordinary message containing a supported text part plus an unsupported part retains its supported text and emits a fixed bounded labeled health warning containing no private message/path text.
Repeating that partial export still emits the health warning and does not invent ingestion errors or additional stored events.
No test duplicates the P071 parser identity/role/timestamp/duplicate/reordering cases.
